x: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the many illegal cesses and kept only the four Sharia taxes: kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams. The other sets include non-Sharia items such as ghari, charai, haq-i-sharb (cesses), taccavi (loans) and iqta or inam (land assignments).

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the ulema interpreted the Sharia and wanted a say in state policy. Statement 3 is wrong: Sultans treated them differently, Firoz Tughlaq relying on them while Alauddin Khalji shut them out. So 1 and 2 only.

Islam reached Andhra with Malik Kafur's campaign of 1310 and with Muhammad bin Tughlaq (MBT). MBT is a Sultan, not a Gulbarga khanqah, and Islam did not arrive only with the Qutb Shahis or after the rise of Vijayanagara.

Sultan Garhi was built by Iltutmish as the tomb of his son Nasiruddin Mahmud. The Red Palace was Balban's palace, the Jamat Khana Masjid was built by Alauddin Khalji, and Firoz Shah Kotla was Firoz Tughlaq's citadel at Firozabad, so the other pairs are wrong.
The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).

Tradition credits Amir Khusrau with the sitar, the tabla and forms such as tarana and khayal. Statement 4 is wrong: the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music is the Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375), which is not his work. So 1, 2 and 3 only.

Aiman (Yaman), along with Zilaf and Sazgiri, is a raga traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau. Rag Vibodh is by Somnath, Man Kautuhal by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior, and Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music, not Barani's work.

Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar was three storeys high, decorated with glazed tiles and had a huge library. Item 4 is wrong: it followed a Persian (Herat/Samarkand) model; the Cordoba comparison belongs to the Gulbarga Jama Masjid. So 1, 2 and 3 only.

Zain-ul-Abidin had the Mahabharata and Kalhana's Rajatarangini translated into Persian. Mirat-i-Sikandari is a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate by Sikandar bin Muhammad, and Riyaz-us-Salatin is a chronicle of Bengal; neither was a translation under him.

Baz Bahadur's Palace, Rupmati's Pavilion and Ashrafi Mahal belong to the late Malwa period. Hoshang Shah's Tomb (India's first marble tomb) belongs to the early period of Hoshang Shah, who moved the capital from Dhar to Mandu. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
